AddPartTitlesCommand.description: Wire type: AddPartTitles (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

Add titles over several levels in one request: each named level's sweep, as its single-level
command runs it, always book first and each level once, stopping at the first refusal.

Wire type: AddTitles (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

AddVolumeTitlesCommand.description: Wire type: AddVolumeTitles (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

AiServiceStatus.description: Live status of a managed service as the settings UI displays it.

ApiItemType.description:
An item's type as the API reports it: ApiItemType.Narration or ApiItemType.Character
for speech (the speaker decides, ADR-0006), a pause kind by name otherwise.

AppTheme.description: A theme row. The optional colours are null where the palette default applies.

ApplyBookEditsCommand.description: Wire type: ApplyBookEdits (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

AssemblyMessage.description:
`Folder` is the project the (single, global) run belongs to; `OutputFileName` rides on
`Completed`.

AssemblyOutputDto.description:
One assembled audiobook under `<workspace>/{folder}/output/`. CreatedAt is
ISO 8601, UTC: when the file was last written; IsPartial marks a build that skipped
items without audio.

AssemblyState.description: Assembly service state for the connect-time snapshot.

AssemblyStatusDto.description:
`Folder` is the project of the running (or most recent) job, null until the first start;
`OutputFileName` is set once that job has completed and names a file under its assembly outputs.

AttributeItemsCommand.description:
Stamps speaker and voice instructions onto existing items of one paragraph. Item boundaries are
frozen (ADR 0005): this command never creates, deletes, reorders or retypes an item.

Wire type: AttributeItems (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

AttributionChainResponse.description:
The stored chain, plus Resolved (the chain attribution runs: deduped, and the default
config alone when Steps is empty) and every config a step may name.

oneOf.description: Null stores no style: the rung inherits its config's own.

AttributionCountsDto.description: Paragraphs still needing attribution, plus what the queue has in flight for this project.

AttributionPromptStyle.description: Which character-attribution prompt tier an LLM server uses.

AttributionQueueSnapshot.description: The attribution queue's counts and timings, answered by `GET /api/attribution/queue`.

isBusy.description:
Work in hand, globally — one worker drains every folder's queue. Settled outcomes
(Failed/Unfinished) are not busy: those paragraphs are finished.

AudioCountsDto.description: Paragraphs with at least one item still missing audio.

AudioGenMessage.description:
One per AudioGenEvent. Stream group only. `ModelLoading` is not tied to an item:
its `Id` is empty and `Model` names the TTS model loading.

AudioItemOutcomeKind.description:
Why a settled item is not simply done. `Unfinished` exists so
void AudioQueueService.Apply(QueuedAudioItem item, Disposition disposition) can stay total over Disposition: this
queue's phase 1 cannot produce it today (a resolution failure is a `Failed` work outcome,
not empty work), but throwing would break totality and recording it as `Failed` would lie
to the UI chip.

AudioItemRefDto.description:
A speech item audio can be generated for, and the nodes it rolls up into (AudioItemRef on
the wire). An entry of `GET …/nodes/{level}/{id}/item-ids`.

AudioPostProcessStepConfig.description:
One step's config on the settings row: its enabled flag plus JsonElement? AudioPostProcessStepConfig.Settings, the
step's opaque settings payload (shape owned by the step, e.g.
ConsonantSoftenSettings for consonant-soften or SilenceTrimSettings for
silence-trim). The host stores the payload as raw JSON, so the document leaves it unknown and the
step's form narrows it. Order and membership come from
AudioPostProcessStepDefaults, not from the stored list.

AudioProcessingFullResponse.description:
`GET /api/settings/audio-processing/full`: everything the audio-processing settings page shows, in
one read. FfmpegPath is the saved value the form edits; with none saved the app runs
ConfiguredFfmpegPath (the host's `Ffmpeg:Path`), else ffmpeg on PATH.

AudioProcessingSettings.description:
Snapshot of the audio post-processing settings row (`AudioProcessingSettingsService.GetAsync()`),
with defaults already applied for a missing row. FfmpegPath is the ffmpeg every
consumer runs: the SavedFfmpegPath, else the
ConfiguredFfmpegPath, else null (PATH).

AudioQueueSnapshot.description: The audio queue's counts and timings, answered by `GET /api/audio/queue`.

AudioReviewDto.description: AudioReviewInfo on the wire, shared with the live hub's item status; nulls are sent explicitly.

BookCommand.description: Any book command: POST /api/projects/{folder}/commands takes one, chosen by its type.

BookEditItem.description: One AI book edit: the title or item text `Id` names, by `Kind`, set to `NewValue`.

BookEditMessage.description:
One AI book-edit proposal run (Angular ticket 19), sent to the connection that started it.
`Program` is the session id the run belongs to; `Done` carries every row the run landed
(all of them, or the partial set a cancel kept). `Dropped`: a Restore of the project dropped
the session, with the `Reason` to show; sent to the project group, since the session outlives
its runs.

BookEditRowDto.description:
ProposedEdit on the wire; enums as member names. Shared with the REST reads of a
proposal run (`BookEditEndpoints`) on purpose: a row a client got pushed and a row it read
back after missing the push have to be the same shape, or a review screen would need two.
NewValue is null on a `Failed` row.
Sources are in the order the plan names them (empty when it reads none; a missing
source is left out, the reason names it). CanAskAgain is false on a missing-source,
self-source or too-long Failed row, where asking again would only return the same failure.

BookEditRunDto.description: The session's proposal run as a whole — what a client that missed the hub asks for.

BookEditSourceDto.description: One Edit source value a row read: its name (`p1`), the plain label (`Paragraph 1`) and the value.

BookFacets.description:
Which kinds of Book data a mutation changed; a receipt lists each facet it touched. Facets are
facts about the write, not instructions: a reader decides for itself what to reread from them.

BookMutationScope.description:
Whether the affected identifiers on BookMutationEffects are exhaustive.
            BookMutationScope.Exact means they name everything the mutation touched; BookMutationScope.WholeProject
            means they do not, and is the safe answer whenever an implementation cannot enumerate what it
            touched.
            Scope says nothing about whether a targeted refresh is sufficient — that is a read-side
judgement made from the facets as well. An insertion is exact about which Paragraph moved and
still structural.

BookNodeLevel.description: The route segment of node-scoped endpoints (`/nodes/{level}/…`) and of enqueue requests.

BookOverviewDto.description:
Revision: the book revision the read ran against, a reader's baseline for receipts
and snapshots. StructureRules: what may be inserted where, one entry per anchor
kind — the node menu renders from it.

BookStructuralRelation.description:
A split or merge stated as a relationship between two nodes, so a reader can carry expansion
from the node that disappeared to the one that took its place.

BulkAssignPreviewDto.description:
BulkAssignPreview on the wire: what a bulk assign over the ids would write.
Paragraphs without Character items count in neither number.

BulkAssignPreviewRequest.description: The body of `POST …/characters/bulk-assign-preview`: the paragraphs to preview.

ChapterVoicePreviewDto.description: A row of `GET …/characters/{id}/voice-rules/preview`: the voice a character's rules pick at the start of a chapter; null when none resolves.

CharacterLineDto.description: One item a character speaks, with where it sits so the reader can open there.

CharacterSeriesLinkDto.description: A Character's series link on the Cast page's roster; bool CharacterSeriesLinkDto.Differs: this book's Voices are not the series copy (#222).

CharacterSummaryDto.description:
A cast-list row. bool CharacterSummaryDto.NarratesBook is true on the character the narrator link
points at; bool CharacterSummaryDto.IsNarrator marks the seed Narrator row itself. CharacterSeriesLinkDto? CharacterSummaryDto.SeriesLink is its
Series character when it is series-linked (ADR 0018), else null. Aliases carry their ids so the detail
can offer removal directly.

CheckpointState.description: How the user settled a Pipeline step's confirmed checkpoint. No row means open.

ClearBookContentCommand.description: Wire type: ClearBookContent (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

ConfigThroughput.description:
One config's share of a Throughput Run. Keyed by config id, never by name: a config renamed
mid-run stays one row, and the display name is resolved at render.

configId.description: The serving config's id — the row's identity.

configName.description: The name last seen on a RequestStarted, for render convenience only.

generationMs.description: Σ `predicted_ms` over the same requests, or null if none did.

requests.description: Requests this config served in the run, whether or not they reported timings.

tokensOut.description: Σ `predicted_n` over the requests that reported timings, or null if none did.

tokensPerSecond.description:
This config's Run Throughput: `Σ predicted_n ÷ Σ predicted_ms`. Null when nothing
measurable arrived — never `0`, which would mean "it generated nothing".

ContextItemDto.description:
An item in a context paragraph. string? ContextItemDto.Speaker is the character's name on a dialog
item, null when the item is dialog whose speaker is not yet attributed; narration items are
not dialog and carry no speaker.

CreateCharacterAndAssignCommand.description:
"New character…" from the speaker menu in one request: resolves `Name` as
CreateCharacterCommand does (an existing name or alias answers with its own id), then
stamps that character on exactly one target — `ItemId` as SetItemCharacterCommand,
`ParagraphId` as SetParagraphCharacterCommand, or `ParagraphIds` as
SetParagraphsCharacterCommand. Answers the character's id.

Wire type: CreateCharacterAndAssign (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

CreateCharacterCommand.description: Wire type: CreateCharacter (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

CreateVoiceCommand.description: Wire type: CreateVoice (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

CreateVoiceRuleCommand.description: Wire type: CreateVoiceRule (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteChapterCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteChapter (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteCharacterCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteCharacter (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteParagraphCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteParagraph (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteParagraphItemCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteParagraphItem (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeletePartCommand.description: Wire type: DeletePart (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteVoiceCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteVoice (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteVoiceRuleCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteVoiceRule (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DeleteVolumeCommand.description: Wire type: DeleteVolume (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

DiscoveredCharacterDto.description:
ExistingCharacterId names the roster character the row resolves onto (by its name or
alias, as apply resolves it) — the review's "Already exists" row.

DiscoveryOutcomeDto.description:
IReadOnlyList<string> DiscoveryOutcomeDto.Collisions: names or aliases two characters would own once every row is
applied (AliasCollisions). Advisory; the client recomputes as rows are edited.

DiscoveryStatus.description:
How character discovery ended. An answer never carries `NoLlmConfigured`: the endpoint
turns it into a 422.

DismissAudioReviewCommand.description: Wire type: DismissAudioReview (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

EditPlanStatus.description:
How planning an AI book edit ended. The planner answers all but EditPlanStatus.NoTargets,
which the caller sets when the plan parsed but its scope matched no items. `Ok` is the only
status that carries a program; the rest explain why there is nothing to do.

EscalationState.description: The latched "escalating N items → config (step S)" label; null when no escalation is active.

FfmpegProbeResult.description: Outcome of an ffmpeg probe. string FfmpegProbeResult.Message carries the version banner or the error.

ffmpegPath.description: Persisted before the probe; blank means "rely on PATH".

referenceSeconds.description: The stored take's length, as VoiceDto reports it.

referenceWarning.description: Set over the 15 s soft Reference Limit: the take was kept.

HistoryBusyDto.description: Why the project can't be viewed at a step or restored right now: what is queued or running for it.

HistoryDto.description:
A project's History (`GET /api/projects/{folder}/history`): its steps newest first, the step the
Head points at, what keeps it busy (null when idle) and whether a Restore is in progress.

HistoryMessage.description:
`StepLanded` | `StepChanged` | `StepClosed`: a step that appeared in a project's
History, an open one a later commit extended, or one that closed, with its row as
`GET /api/projects/{folder}/history` lists it. Sent to the project group. A step recorded by
one mutation lands and closes together, so both arrive back to back.
`BusyChanged` carries no step: the project's busy reason ("Attribution: 128 paragraphs left")
moved, or went null when the project went idle. A busy project can't be viewed at a step.
`Restoring`: a Restore of the project `Phase` started or finished; `Finished` carries
the Restore step it added, or no step when it added none or failed. Writes are refused in between.

HistoryStep.description: One History step as History lists it (context/history.md). int HistoryStep.Sequence is for display only: the line of steps is the Guid? HistoryStep.ParentStepId chain from the Head, so nothing assumes the highest sequence is the tip (ADR 0016). string? HistoryStep.Note says what is unusual about the step, or is null: "part 2" when another commit split its scope, how a Background run ended early ("212 of 340 paragraphs, cancelled"), or "interrupted" when the app stopped while it was open — joined by " · ", without brackets.DateTimeOffset? HistoryStep.EndedAt is when the step closed, or, while it is open, its last change. An interrupted step keeps the time of its last change: when it really ended is not known. bool HistoryStep.IsOpen, not DateTimeOffset? HistoryStep.EndedAt, says whether it is open.HistoryStepKind HistoryStep.Kind says what opened the step, and StepAction? HistoryStep.Action what kind of action a request's or Background run's step is (null on the others): the History sheet picks a row's icon from them, never from the label, so renaming a label changes no icon.Guid? HistoryStep.RestoredFromStepId is the step a Restore step brought back; null for any other. bool HistoryStep.CantOpen marks a step that can no longer be opened (its old schema fails to migrate).

HistoryStepDto.description:
One History step as `GET /history` lists it (`GET /history/{stepId}` answers one), plus
RestorePreview, what a Restore to it would cost now — null for a step that can't be
opened, and so can't be restored.

HistoryStepKind.description: What opened a History step: a request, a Background run, a Restore, History starting, or an import.

InsertNodeCommand.description:
Creates one node beside or inside the anchor; its kind follows from the anchor and the
Placement InsertNodeCommand.Placement. A new Paragraph is born holding `Text` as one unattributed Speech
item — never empty, because an empty Paragraph reads as a pause. A new Speech item at a
Paragraph's start or end holds `Text` too, born unattributed. `Title` is for a new
Volume, Part or Chapter.

Wire type: InsertNode (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

InsertParagraphItemCommand.description:
Creates one Speech ParagraphItem next to `AnchorItemId`, inside the anchor's own Paragraph.
The new item is born unattributed — no speaker, no voice instructions, no audio: by construction
the anchor held two speakers, so inheriting its speaker would stamp a confident wrong answer that
looks attributed and never reaches the attribution queue.

Wire type: InsertParagraphItem (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

InsertPauseParagraphCommand.description: Wire type: InsertPauseParagraph (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

InsertPosition.description:
Where a new node lands relative to the anchor node it is inserted against.
Shared by the item and pause insertion commands (InsertNodeCommand takes a
Placement); the member names are also the JSON wire values.

ItemAttribution.description:
One item's attribution, ready to apply: the item is addressed by id, and the speaker is already
            resolved to a character id (null = unknown, which never erases an existing stamp).
            Not to be confused with AttributedItem, the wire answer the LLM sends (index + speaker
name); this is the resolved apply-side record.

ItemStatusEntry.description: What the audio queue and the review mirror say about one item.

ItemStatusMessage.description:
Per-paragraph attribution and per-item audio status deltas for one project (debounced). A null entry
means the queue forgot the paragraph or item.

ItemVoiceDto.description:
The Voice a speech item will be spoken in. string? ItemVoiceDto.VoiceName is null when no Voice
resolves; string? ItemVoiceDto.NarratedBy is the linked narrator's name on a narration item. An entry of
`GET …/nodes/Chapter/{id}/voices`.

ItemsEnqueueRequest.description: The body of `POST …/audio/enqueue-items`: an explicit item selection or a single retry. Ids that name no item are ignored.

LiveMessageMap.description: Each /hubs/live family (connection.on name) and the payload it carries.

LiveSnapshot.description: Answer to `GetSnapshot`: singleton state plus one ProjectSnapshot per joined project.

LlmMessage.description: `Delta` is a 100 ms batch of thinking + content text. Stream group only.

apiKey.description: Optional bearer token sent as Authorization header.

attributionBatchSize.description:
Character paragraphs sent per attribution request. 1 = one paragraph per request;
greater values batch consecutive unassigned character paragraphs into a single prompt.

model.description: Optional model id. Omitted from the request when null/blank.

promptStyle.description:
Which attribution prompt tier this server uses. Simple = explicit-tag-only prompt,
for small models that would otherwise guess a speaker instead of escalating.

supportsModelSwitch.description:
True when this endpoint can switch the loaded model on demand (llama.cpp router with
`--models-max 1` autoload). Gates the switch-and-wait model-load path; non-switchable
endpoints (remote OpenAI-compatible servers) leave this false.

LlmTestMessage.description:
How the LLM settings test send ended (Angular ticket 21), sent to the connection that started it.
The tokens themselves travel on `stream:llm`.

connectionId.description: The live hub connection that receives the run's `llmTest` message.

ManualImportRequest.description:
`POST /api/projects/{folder}/import/manual` body: how to re-split the source file by hand
(the manual reread dialog's form, on the wire). `volume` is read only when
`hasMultipleVolumes`, `part` only when `hasMultipleParts`; `chapter` always.
400 when a switched-on level lacks a rule.

MergeChapterCommand.description: Wire type: MergeChapter (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MergeCharactersCommand.description: Wire type: MergeCharacters (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MergeParagraphCommand.description: Wire type: MergeParagraph (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MergeParagraphItemCommand.description: Wire type: MergeParagraphItem (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MergePartCommand.description: Wire type: MergePart (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MergeVolumeCommand.description: Wire type: MergeVolume (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

MoveVoiceRuleCommand.description: Wire type: MoveVoiceRule (the record name minus Command). The folder comes from the route, never the body.

NarrationReleasePreviewDto.description:
NarrationReleasePreview on the wire: what a Release narration over the scope would write.
Paragraphs are the paragraphs it releases and ItemsWithAudio the
items whose audio it discards. For a Chapter or Part, SpeechMarkers are the markers
that passed (count descending, then marker); empty for a Paragraph and when nothing passes.

NarrationReleasePreviewRequest.description:
The body of `POST …/narration/release-preview`: the scope a Release narration would cover; the same
shape as the command, minus its type.

NarrationReleaseScope.description:
Where a ReleaseNarrationCommand reaches. Its own enum rather than
BookNodeLevel: that one has Volume, and a whole-book release is excluded on purpose.

NarratorDto.description:
Who narrates the book, projected from NarratorIdentity — the raw link
column never goes on the wire. Unlinked serialises as
NarratorIdentity NarratorIdentity.Unlinked (the seed row's id, "Narrator", false), so
there is no null case at either end.

NodeChildrenDto.description: Exactly one of the three lists is present, chosen by the requested level.

NodeKind.description: Which kind of node an InsertNodeCommand anchors on. Also the JSON wire values.

NodeStatusMessage.description:
Per-node roll-up deltas for one project (debounced, group `project:{folder}`). A null value
means the node no longer rolls up (the folder was cleared or re-seeded without it).

NodeStatusSummaryDto.description:
NodeStatusSummary on the wire: paragraph counts under one volume/part/chapter. The
service's value is a struct, which the document can only describe with every field optional.

NotTheSameRequest.description: Not the same: a suggested cell (`seriesCharacterId`, `folder`, `characterId`) or a suggested row (`members`).

ParagraphAttributionStatusDto.description:
Queue state only. Attribution results are per item now — read them from the book endpoint's
paragraph items, which carry the stamped character.

ParagraphContextDto.description: A paragraph with its nearest neighbours in the same chapter, nearest last in IReadOnlyList<ContextParagraphDto> ParagraphContextDto.Before and first in IReadOnlyList<ContextParagraphDto> ParagraphContextDto.After.

ParagraphDto.description: bool ParagraphDto.IsPauseParagraph: no items, or a single pause item.

ParagraphItemDto.description:
string ParagraphItemDto.OrderKey is the item's fractional position key within its paragraph (items
arrive already in that order). ApiItemType ParagraphItemDto.ItemType stays for older clients; new ones read
bool ParagraphItemDto.IsPause and the speaker.

ParagraphRefDto.description:
A Character paragraph and the nodes it rolls up into — what a selection holds per row. An entry of
`GET …/nodes/{level}/{id}/paragraph-ids`.

ParagraphStatusEntry.description: What the attribution queue currently says about one paragraph; null fields mean "nothing".

ParagraphTtsServiceConfig.description:
A configured paragraph-TTS backend. Common identity lives in columns; all
backend-specific settings are serialized into string ParagraphTtsServiceConfig.SettingsJson,
keyed by ParagraphTtsServiceType ParagraphTtsServiceConfig.Type. New backend types stay additive.

ParagraphTtsServiceType.description: Selects the paragraph-TTS backend and its settings shape.

ParagraphTtsSettingsSchema.description: The fields a TTS provider type exposes, with the recommended default per field.

ParagraphsEnqueueRequest.description: The body of `POST …/attribution/enqueue-paragraphs`: an explicit selection. Ids that are not Character paragraphs are ignored.

PauseDurationsDto.description:
The assembler's per-kind silences, as one object so a card saves them together;
`PUT /api/settings/audio-processing/pauses` takes the same shape.

Placement.description:
Where an InsertNodeCommand puts its new node: Placement.Before / Placement.After
name a sibling at the anchor's own level, Placement.AtStart / Placement.AtEnd a first or
last child one level down — never two levels down. The member names are also the JSON wire values.

thinking.description: Let the model think before planning — slower, better on vague instructions and at choosing between template tokens and an LLM; on unless set false.

PlanBookEditResponse.description:
Status is the planner's EditPlanStatus, or `NoTargets` when the
plan parsed but matched nothing. Only `Ok` carries a Program, the opaque session
id every later call names. Transform is the plan's TransformKind: only
`Llm` plans send requests per item, so only they have a RequestCount above 0
(the LLM requests the proposal will send) and offer per-row retries.

PreflightConflictDto.description: A running GPU service the task does not need; stopped first to free VRAM.

PreflightMessage.description:
One pre-flight run (Angular ticket 25), sent to the connection that started it. `Stage`
carries a service and its stage; `Done` carries `Ok` and, on failure, the summary
`Reason`. `Run` is the id the 202 answered with.

PreflightPlanDto.description: `ready` means nothing to start and nothing to stop: the task may run now.

connectionId.description: The live hub connection that receives the run's `preflight` messages.

PreflightRunResponse.description: 202 with the run id; every message of the run carries it.

PreflightServiceDto.description: A required service that is not Ready, with its status.

PreviewStageDto.description: bool PreviewStageDto.Applied false means the step fell back to its input; string? PreviewStageDto.Reason says why.

ProjectSeries.description: The series a project is in, as its project reads show it.

ProjectSnapshot.description:
Everything a project group member needs on join: current revision plus full status maps. Answers
`JoinProject`; also an entry of `LiveSnapshot.projects`.

ProjectStatusDto.description:
The whole-project roll-up behind the pipeline stepper and the reader tree badges.
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, NodeStatusSummaryDto> ProjectStatusDto.Nodes is keyed by Volume/Part/Chapter id and is the same map the live hub's
`nodeStatus` deltas patch; IReadOnlyList<Guid> ProjectStatusDto.VolumeIds are in book order. IReadOnlyDictionary<PipelineStep, StepCheckpointDto> ProjectStatusDto.Checkpoints
holds only the steps the user confirmed or skipped, keyed by step id. Served by
`GET /api/projects/{folder}/status`. Item counts are items; Attribution,
Audio and Review count paragraphs, like the node summaries.
Revision is the book revision the reads started at.

ProjectSummary.description:
One row of the project list (`GET /api/projects`). BookFileType? ProjectSummary.FileType is null for a folder
whose DB could not be opened.

oneOf.description: The series the project is in, or null. Filled in by the API from the series registries.

PromptCatalogEntry.description: One prompt kind as the settings pages show it; `Template` is the resolved text.

expectedResponse.description: The JSON shape the LLM must answer with; null for a plain-text prompt (voice).

warnings.description: Compatibility warnings, such as "Stored override missing …".

PronunciationDeleted.description:
`DELETE …/pronunciations/{id}`: what deleting an entry cost, counted as for
PronunciationSaved.

PronunciationDraftRequest.description:
`POST …/pronunciations/impact` body: no Id adds, an Id edits
that entry, Delete deletes it.

PronunciationEntry.description:
One Pronunciation and its reach in the book (`GET /api/projects/{folder}/pronunciations`): how
often its written form matches, in how many items, and how many of those items have audio.

PronunciationImpactReport.description:
What saving a draft would do: its reach (matches, items, items with audio — for a delete, the
entry's reach now), the audio a save discards, the entries it overlaps, the entry it duplicates,
and every match in book order.

PronunciationMatchInBook.description:
One place the draft's written form matches: the item, where it is, and the sentence around it with
where that sentence starts in the item's text (what a try-out names it by), the match's offsets in
that sentence, and the sentence's Spoken text with the drafted list applied, with where the match's
spoken form sits in it (case carried over, as TTS will be asked to say it).

PronunciationOverlap.description:
An entry whose written form holds the draft's as whole words, or is held by it. The longer one wins
where both match, so DraftWins is whether the draft's is the longer.

PronunciationRef.description: An entry of the list, as the impact of a draft names it.

PronunciationSaved.description:
A saved entry with its reach, and what saving it cost: AudioDiscardCount items lost
their audio, and NeedsAudioCount spoken items now have none.

PronunciationSpan.description:
One span of an item's text the list matches: where it is, the entry it names, and where the
sentence around it starts in the item's text (what a try-out names that sentence by).

PronunciationSpanReport.description:
The spans in some chapters, in book order, and the entries they name (each once, by written form):
`GET …/pronunciations/matches?chapterIds=…`.

connectionId.description: The live hub connection that receives the run's `bookEdit` messages.

QueueMessage.description: Both queues' roll-ups plus the attribution escalation banner (debounced, group `global`).

ReceiptEffects.description:
BookMutationEffects on the wire, with IReadOnlyList<BookFacets> ReceiptEffects.Facets as a list of single facets
(never `None` or `All`): a `[Flags]` value would travel as one comma-joined string the
document can't describe.

shield and every tab read one source. Each carries the whole report: the rows (the current step's

last ran (null: not yet).
bool SetupCheckReport.FirstRun: this start created app.db, so the web app opens on the Setup check.

bool SetupCheckReport.NoWorkspace: this host started without a usable Workspace; every other API call
is refused and the web app shows only the Setup check until the app restarts.
SetupFullRun? SetupCheckReport.FullRun: the Full check going on, null when none is. int SetupCheckReport.FullCheckEstimateSeconds:
how long a Full check is likely to take, for its confirm. string? SetupCheckReport.PutBack: after a Full
check, what it did with the containers it drove ("Put back: read2me-whisper stopped again.").

result. Every row carries a fix hint; the page shows it only for rows that aren't Passed or Not used.
bool SetupCheckRow.Managed: the app can start and restart what the row checks — a docker AI service,
or a config whose every URL is one. False for the Workspace and tools, and for a config on a
URL the app doesn't manage. SetupRerun? SetupCheckRow.Rerun: what re-running this one check takes, null
when it can't be (a Quick-tier row, or a config with no active one).

SetupCheckTier.description: Which check judges the row: the Quick check reads, the Full check sends real requests.

SetupFixHint.description:

a command or file path to copy, for things outside the app; null when there is none.

SetupFullRun.description:

doing ("Encoding a 1 s tone to .m4b"). bool SetupFullRun.Cancelling: a cancel was asked for, so the
run stops once this step ends.

one running and loads a model, and the web app confirms first.

but its own anchor here: it takes no speech item at its start or end.

needs text (TextRequired).

ThroughputSnapshot.description:
A read-only view of the current (or last) Throughput Run, pulled by whoever is painting.
Absence is distinguishable from zero at every point: a figure that could not be measured is
null, and a run that never happened has bool ThroughputSnapshot.HasRun false.

generationRate.description: The live figure: output tok/s over a sliding TimeSpan ThroughputSnapshot.GenerationRateWindow of the in-flight request, differenced from consecutive cumulative readings. Null whenever nothing is currently measurable — between requests before the first token, and always once the run has ended, because a frozen "now 87.3 tok/s" beside an idle queue reads as current and is a lie. It says steady vs stuttering and nothing else; the headline is double? ThroughputSnapshot.RunThroughput.

generationRateHistory.description:
The sparkline's history: exactly int ThroughputSnapshot.HistoryBuckets buckets of
int ThroughputSnapshot.HistoryBucketMsms, oldest first, spanning the last
TimeSpan ThroughputSnapshot.HistorySpan of the run. A bucket nothing was measured in is null — an empty
bucket is not a `0` bucket. All null once the run has ended, or before it has
generated anything.

isRunActive.description:
Whether the run is still open. Goes false at RunEnded, at which point live
figures blank while the headline and breakdown below persist — a frozen "now 87.3 tok/s"
beside an idle queue reads as current and is a lie.

perConfig.description:
The run's per-config breakdown, one row per config id that served a request, so an
escalation from a 4b to a 26b doesn't blend into one meaningless average.

runThroughput.description:
The headline: `Σ predicted_n ÷ Σ predicted_ms` across every request in the run,
summing the primitives and dividing once at the end. Null when nothing was measurable.

determines the shape of the type-specific settings blob.

(null on the default rule and on an open "from here on" end); a dangling anchor names a

Progress and the final report go to every live hub client as setupCheck { kind: progress|done, report }. 409 naming the work in flight while the Audio or Character queue holds items, or a voice batch, discovery or assembly runs, and while one check re-runs.
Cancel the Full check: it stops once the current step ends, and the checks it hadn't reached read Not run. 202 with the report (fullRun.cancelling true); 409 when none is running.

Run the Quick check (Workspace, ffmpeg, docker CLI) and answer the new report. It never starts, stops or switches anything; it creates the Workspace folder when missing. While a Full check runs it answers the run's report instead.
